explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares GPT-4 judgments with human evaluations on the same set of instances, reporting agreement between human annotators' majority labels and GPT-4 evaluation results.

prompts.notes: Full prompt text provided in Figure (Appendix B.2). GPT-4 is asked to select which output would receive more upvotes in the given subreddit using A/B testing framework.

human_eval_details.num_evaluators: at least 3 per subreddit (3-6 total, with top 3 selected based on agreement)

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: reasonable given the difficulty and subjectivity of the task

guidelines.notes: Full guidelines and annotation interface provided in Appendix A. Annotators browse subreddits for 10-15 minutes before annotating.

shared_criteria: Likelihood of receiving upvotes in subreddit

sample_size.notes: All 717 human annotations across 8 subreddits were compared with GPT-4 evaluation results

quantitative_scores.notes: Human annotators' majority labels agreed with GPT-4 evaluation results 69.8% of the time

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 evaluations achieved 69.8% agreement with human majority labels on identifying responses more likely to receive upvotes in specific subreddits.

shared_criteria: Likelihood of receiving upvotes in subreddit
criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM and human evaluated the primary criterion of which response would receive more upvotes. Human evaluators additionally flagged gibberish/repetitive outputs which was not part of the GPT-4 evaluation.
